title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Oct. 27
gist: A title-only roundup of seven new semiconductor research papers: imec on 3D volumetric DRAM-on-GPU thermal limits beyond HBM, multi-tier CFET self-heating, a 200G/λ slow-light silicon modulator with reduced DSP, dry-deposited EUV/e-beam resists, NN-based SPICE modeling, security-aware 3D compute-in-memory mapping, and a Pt-W high-NA EUV mask absorber. No results or data are given beyond titles and one-line headlines.

insights.claim: imec has published a thermal design envelope for 3D volumetric DRAM stacked directly on GPUs, framed as going beyond today's HBM-on-GPU integration and expanding the thermal design space.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Research attention on DRAM-on-GPU signals a possible post-HBM memory architecture that could reshape the memory/packaging value chain.
insights.quote: Vertical DRAM Stacking Expands Thermal Design Space Beyond HBM-on-GPU

insights.claim: TU Munich and IIT Kanpur report that self-heating and parasitic effects challenge the scaling of multi-tier CFET transistors.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Thermal and parasitic limits could slow CFET adoption roadmaps at leading-edge nodes.
insights.quote: Self-Heating And Parasitics Challenge Multi-Tier CFET Scaling

insights.claim: A Chinese Academy of Sciences-led paper finds a Pt-W alloy shows potential as a thinner low-n absorber for high-NA EUV masks.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Indicates Chinese research activity in high-NA EUV mask materials despite export controls.
insights.quote: Pt-W Alloy Shows Potential For Thinner High-NA EUV Mask Absorbers

insights.claim: KU Leuven, Kunsan, VUB and imec report that a dry-deposited halogenated zeolitic imidazolate framework resist shows different tone behavior under EUV versus e-beam exposure.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Dry resists are an emerging alternative to spin-on resists relevant to EUV materials suppliers.

insights.claim: Researchers from Institute of Science Tokyo, Yokohama National University, AIST and PETRA demonstrate a slow-light silicon modulator reaching 200 Gb/s PAM4 per wavelength with reduced DSP via a built-in electro-optic equalizer.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Cutting DSP power in 200G/lane optics supports the shift to optical interconnects in AI data centers.

insights.claim: TU Munich proposes neural-network-based transistor modeling for ultra-fast SPICE simulation and standard cell library characterization, and ASU/University of Maryland propose SEAL, multitenant security-aware layer mapping for heterogeneous 3D compute-in-memory accelerators.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: ML-accelerated EDA and multitenant security for CiM are active research fronts that may feed into commercial tools.
